p: "Rejoice and be glad on Simchas Torah,
for its merchandise is better than all merchandise"
"Merchandise" refers to the means and the effort
before he reaches the substance of the business,
and commerce in the matters of this world,
toil and make arrangements and efforts
and all his toil will have been for nothing.
even if he has not yet attained
in order to attain the goal —
this itself is counted as receiving reward
in the very substance of Torah study.
כִּי חַיִּים הוּא לָנוּ עוֹז וְאוֹרָה:
"For it is life for us, strength and light":
for through the Torah there is the power
"Strength" is the aspect of the force
"Who is mighty? He who conquers his yetzer";
and this is through the power of the Torah,
I created the Torah as its antidote."
And "light" is that through the Torah
the darkness becomes light for a person —
the darkness the yetzer hara casts over a person
into thinking that he is doing a mitzvah thereby;
עַל וַיֵּאָבֵק אִישׁ עִמּוֹ (בְּרֵאשִׁית לב, כה)
on "And a man wrestled with him" (Bereishis 32:25),
that he appeared to him as a talmid chacham;
for he comes to mislead him in this way,
appearing to him as his rebbi
who teaches him wisdom for his benefit.
And through the Torah it becomes light for a person,
so that he not be caught in the trap
of the one who makes darkness into light.
וְיֵשׁ לְרַמֵּז זֶה בַּפָּסוּק (דְּבָרִים לב, ב)
And one can find this alluded to in the pasuk (Devarim 32:2),
"My teaching shall drop as the rain,
my word shall distill as the dew,"
on account of the aspects mentioned above
that are found in the power of the Torah.
alludes to the strength and force
that entices toward what is forbidden;
for "ya'arof" is an expression of killing,
"and they shall break the neck of the calf";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and as it says of David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
(Tehillim 109:22), "and my heart is slain within me,"
for he had killed the yetzer hara like one slain.
that illuminates the dark places of the yetzer hara;
כִּי טַל אוֹרוֹת טַלֶּךָ (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, יט)
for "a dew of lights is your dew" (Yeshayahu 26:19)
is the dew with which He will in the future
that is, those who in their lifetime are called dead,
for what seems to him to be life
"Once he sinned and repeated it, it becomes to him as permitted";
and through the dew of lights
it will become clear to him that he is standing
in the darkness of the yetzer hara,
and with the dew of Torah He will revive him
from going down to the pit.
